headline: Keep the meeting that ends earliest
statement: Return the minimum number of intervals to remove so that the remaining intervals do not overlap. Intervals whose end equals another start are compatible.
intuition: Keep as many non-overlapping intervals as possible, then remove the rest. Choose the interval that ends earliest because it leaves the most room for future intervals. Repeat among intervals starting after the chosen end. Sorting by start alone would not guarantee this best choice.
approach: Keep each interval whose start is at least the last retained end.
Count retained intervals and subtract from the total.
correctness: For a best possible compatible schedule, replace its first interval with the globally earliest-finishing interval. The replacement ends no later, so all later choices remain compatible. Repeating the argument on the remaining timeline proves greedy selects a maximum-cardinality compatible set. Removing the complement is minimal.
bruteForce: List every subset, check pairwise overlap, and retain the largest compatible subset.

pitfalls: Sort by end rather than start.
